messages:
marta: Heads-up — multiple enterprise customers in APAC reported their requests getting routed to us-east after an apparent healthcheck flap. They saw higher p99 and billing surprises. I pasted a minimal repro and agent logs below. Can eng-platform take a look?

marta: Repro (customer says this is repeatable):
```bash
# from customer VPC in ap-southeast-1
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# response returns 200 from node id: node-09-us-east-1
```

marta: Support agent pulled probe logs — the probe shows a short 503 then 200, but the routing decision swapped to us-east within ~18s of the 503. Probe agent id: probe-az1-ap-3, agent ver: 2.4.1

marta: snippet from probe-agent log:
```
[2026-02-12T03:14:05Z] PROBE agent=probe-az1-ap-3 region=ap-southeast-1 target=api.redwood.example.com status=200 latency_ms=120
[2026-02-12T03:14:12Z] PROBE agent=probe-az1-ap-3 region=ap-southeast-1 target=api.redwood.example.com status=503 latency_ms=10 reason=upstream-reset
[2026-02-12T03:14:20Z] PROBE agent=probe-az1-ap-3 region=ap-southeast-1 target=api.redwood.example.com status=200 latency_ms=110
[2026-02-12T03:14:23Z] ROUTER decision=failover from=ap-southeast-1 to=us-east-1 cause=healthcheck_threshold
```

marta: Customer says they did NOT see any config change or deployment during that window. They are on Dedicated; they expect region affinity.

josh: Looking. Quick hypothesis: probe transient 503 triggered immediate failover because router uses consecutive-failures=1 for that pool. That would be... aggressive. Do we have rollout where policy got overwritten?

alex: We shipped an emergency probe-change last month for noisy connections — it reverted retry-window from 60s to 15s for some pools. Might explain quick flip. Will check which pools got the new policy.

priya: Customer impact: two customers reported requests billed at cross-region egress rates for the hour after failover. They've opened billing tickets. They want replay logs and a rollback if this was a config push.

josh: Can we confirm router logs for that customer id? If router saw the failing probe from ap-southeast-1, it should evaluate fallback policy and region affinity weight. Something else: NAT IP rotation on the probe host could make the probe appear from a different public ASN, and we have an anti-affinity rule that marks unknown ASNs as lower-affinity.

marta: I pulled router trace for the customer session id=ce-9921:
```
ROUTER TRACE session=ce-9921 time=2026-02-12T03:14:24Z from_region=ap-southeast-1 selected=us-east-1 reason=probe_failover (policy: immediate_failover, fallback_variant=low-latency-without-affinity)
```

marta: Probe host NAT log shows ip change at 03:14:11 which aligns with the 503. NAT rotated to a new elastic IP advertised from a different peering.

alex: That lines up. We recently enabled short TTL floating IPs for cost optimization in ap-southeast. That change can cause probe-to-router ASN mismatch. Need to revert short-ttl or add stable probe source ips.

josh: Short-term mitigation: increase consecutive-failures threshold for Dedicated region-affinity pools to 3 and extend the health-window to 60s. That avoids 1-off 503 causing instant failover. Long-term: pin probe source IPs per region or enrich probe with stable region-auth header so router trusts origin.

dani: Noted billing impact. I'll create a bill-job to estimate cross-region egress costs and queue refunds if threshold exceeded. Assigning to billing-team-queue.

ops-bot: Deployments detected: config-change:region-fallback-policy applied to pool:dedicated-ap-southeast at 2026-02-12T02:58:10Z by deploy-bot (change-id cf-7782).

priya: Ok, looks like that deploy matches alex's emergency change. Customer-facing reply: telling them we identified a config change and are rolling a fix; refund/billing follow-up.

josh: Action items:
- ENG-PLATFORM: revert cf-7782 for dedicated-ap-southeast or patch policy to consecutive_failures=3 (josh)
- INFRA: pin probe IPs or mark probe-source-as-stable for ap-southeast (alex)
- SUPPORT: send preliminary message to customers, include repro, ETA for fix (priya)
- BILLING: estimate impact and prepare credits (dani)

marta: I'm on customer comms. Will attach the router trace and probe logs. ETA for customer update: 30m.

alex: I'll open rollback PR now and target rollback to 2026-02-12T04:00Z if ops approves.

josh: If rollback not possible, we can hotpatch policy via feature-flag. Also adding a short-term tweak: don't evaluate region affinity for sessions that recently had a healthy 200 in same region within last 2 min. That would prevent flip after brief 503.

priya: Customer update sent. Marking as P1 escalation.

marta: Thanks all. I'll update thread after rollback outcome.

— 30m later —

marta: Rollback applied at 2026-02-12T04:01:10Z. Early signals: no new cross-region failovers in the last 10m for the impacted pools. Customer acknowledged and asked for post-mortem.

josh: Great. Next steps: postmortem with timeline, decision to pin probe IPs vs stable-region-header, and add a test that simulates probe NAT rotation to ensure policy tolerance.

marta: Filing postmortem and assigning to eng-platform + infra. Closing support ticket after billing follow-up.
